entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Thank you for stopping by. Sorry it had[n]to be after such a long day of classes...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Help yourself to some snacks,[n]if you'd like.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Well then, let's get started.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: So... you're currently staying with[n]a friend of your parents, correct?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: How are the digs there? No trouble[n]at home, I take it?
Pretty much.
I try not to think about it.
His curry is to die for.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I see.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I'm glad someone considerate was there[n]for you when you needed it.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Is that so...?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Well, I'd say it's an understandable[n]approach.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Oh, he's a good cook?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: ...Now that you mention it, I could go[n]for some curry myself.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: It's been roughly a month since you[n]transferred here, right?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: How's school life been?
The usual.
The teachers seem distant.
My morning commute sucks.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I see... Well, at the very least, it hasn't[n]been exceptionally bad.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: ...That's most likely because the teachers[n]are extra-skittish around the students[n]right now.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I can relate—the Ginza Line jolts around[n]quite a bit.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Sorry, I'm more scientifically-minded[n]than rhetorically, so I'm not sure if[n]this is the best way to put it, but...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: You're staying in a new city, away from[n]any family, but your record's followed[n]you here and spread across the school...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: You can see why people could be[n]concerned for your well-being, right?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Would you say you've found a place[n]where you belong yet, since relocating?
Somewhere I belong...

entries.speaker: Morgana
entries.en: Now then, this is the official formation of[n]the Phantom Thieves organization!
I do now.
It's still pretty new to me, but...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Really?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: New...?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: So you're saying there is somewhere[n]you feel like you belong?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Thank goodness. I'm sure Sadayo—

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I mean, Ms. Kawakami will be happy[n]to hear it.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Oh that's right, the snacks! There's no[n]need to be modest here—I have both[n]sweet and salty options.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: In fact, I believe I'll have an apple juice[n]myself.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I have to admit—I only know the gist of[n]things from what they reported on the[n]news, but I am familiar with your record.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: This may be an odd question, but...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Is that really how it happened?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Know what? Never mind. This is a[n]pretty sensitive topic, and we don't[n]need to go there now.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: It's just...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: And anyway, I'm still a counselor at heart.[n]I can tell, just from this little chat...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: You're not the kind of person who[n]would assault a random stranger[n]because you didn't like his face.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Sorry, I know I shouldn't be speculating,[n]especially now...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: This is turning into more of an[n]interrogation than a counseling[n]session, am I right?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Look at the time—we should wrap[n]things up for today.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Before you leave, though, I have[n]one last question...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Are you close with Yoshizawa-san?
We're just acquaintances.
What about her?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Ah, that explains you two chatting[n]earlier.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Oh, well, I only ask because I saw you[n]chatting with her earlier...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: If you don't mind, could you check in[n]on her from time to time?

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: The teachers have a close eye on her for[n]their own reasons, but she seems to have[n]lost an interest in everyday student life.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: For instance, she told me she plans to[n]skip the cleanup event tomorrow.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: She didn't tell me anything of the sort[n]directly, but I can tell she's focusing[n]on a pretty big goal at the moment.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: I'm basically an outsider here, so I have[n]no intention of telling her she has to[n]attend the cleanup...

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Even still, I can't overlook her passing[n]up opportunities at healthy student life.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Ah— Sorry again! Look at me rambling[n]just as I said I was going to wrap this up.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: Thank you so much for coming today.[n]I hope you'll come again if you decide[n]you need to.

entries.speaker: Maruki
entries.en: See ya around.
